W1 · density · re-run of the frozen prompt

One row of six moved the chart 159px up. Nothing else moved.

Lane D changed one snippet — the bento template's lead group, four display tiles at data-c="3" → six compact tiles at data-c="1". This page re-runs the #246 lane-B protocol on that library: the same prompt, blind then sighted, the same fence, the same measurement, the same instrument re-run on the #246 pages so the numbers are comparable. The sighted page's first chart starts at 678.6px against the baseline's 837.8px at 1440 light; the six tiles and the whole chart canvas are above a 900px fold, where the baseline showed four tiles and a cut chart. Seed 1 (the 2×2 board) does not recur. The other five seeds recur, exactly as the plan predicts — they belong to W2–W5. Richness is unchanged at 2/2/0/2: the edit packs the same content, it does not add any.

DP-21signalOne channel per tier, and no tier is identified by a conjunction. Predator: hue + glyph (+ motion only if the reader must act before leaving the page). Blood and fruit: the ruled red or green ink on the numeral with its symbol, nothing else coloured. Game: enclosure and position — a button, a count, a row at the top — never hue. DP-22signalColour follows meaning, not arithmetic: every metric declares which direction is good, and the red/green ink and spark stroke bind to good/bad, never to up/down. DP-23signalMotion is the rarest signal, reserved for a change that happened while the reader was looking — an item arrived, an action completed — and never spent on load or entry choreography on a monitoring page. Hover motion is an affordance, not a signal, and stays.missedL327 figure.dv.dv-animate: the chart-line draws on load (drive chart_legend_toggle.animName cn-chart-line-dvDraw); the spark ends fade in — entry choreography on a monitoring page
DP-24signalSize and position carry importance; hue carries state; weight carries reading order. A tile is never coloured to say "important", and never enlarged to say "wrong".metsix equal lead tiles L240-306 (data-c="1"), colour only on rag/delta; no tile coloured for importance or enlarged for wrongness
DP-25signalMono's law gets an id: in the mono theme every hue outside the neutral ramp is a signal by definition — the ruled RAG inks and fills, the brand red on the primary action — and a hue with no state behind it is a defect, not a style.n/athe mono rule has no id yet (Q9, Dave's); the observable hue census is DP-20's row. Chart series hues L446 (--data-series-1..3) are the dataviz kit's ruled palette, outside the row's stated scope
DP-26signalCopy carries the same tiers. A status is one word, an adjective or past participle ("Held", "Returned", "Due"); an action is verb-first ("Approve", "Release", "Retry"); the word and the colour agree in tier; no decoration adjectives, intensifiers or exclamation marks anywhere on the board.missedL485 'Returned' is one past participle; L481 'Approval due 18:00' and L489 'Due 30 Sep' are phrases; L283 '5 need you' is a sentence in a status slot
DP-27signalQuiet is a designed state, not an absence. The all-clear reads as one line of default ink — "Nothing needs you" — with no green tick and no celebratory colour; the cockpit stays dark when things are good.missedL146 .status.ok green dot on 'All nostro feeds up to date' — a green tick on a quiet fact
DP-28localityAn action lives on the surface it acts on. A control that changes one module sits in that module's own header or footer; a control that changes the whole page sits in the page title zone; a control that finalises a flow sits in the flow's action bar. The distance between a control and its consumer is an edge ( triggeredBy / groupsWith ), and a control whose consumer is on another surface — or has none — is misplaced.missedL151 currency filter in the page title zone; its consumer is the grid in hidden tab p2 (glue L1652); no triggeredBy/groupsWith edge names it
DP-29localityFeedback appears at the locus of attention. First on the control that was operated (state, count, inline message), then on the object that changed (row updates or leaves); a toast is used only when the effect is out of view; an error that must be acted on is shown inline at the field and summarised at the top when the field may be off-screen. Feedback never lives only in a corner the eye is not in.missedfiltering from the Overview tab: the chip and count land in #fbar/#dgCount inside hidden p2 (drive filter_usd count '7 results' only visible after #t2) — feedback out of the locus of attention

07 · Findings

Each one a fact with its probe

  1. The edit moved the sighted page exactly as much as it moved the snippet: −159.2px. Chart group top 837.8 → 678.6 at 1440 light (probe-render.json vs …baseline-reprobe/arm-B/probe-reprobe.json, same script). Six tiles and the full chart canvas sit above a 900px fold; the baseline showed four and a cut canvas.
  2. Seed 1 passes; richness does not move. 2/2/0/2 before and after on the sighted arm. Density re-packs the same content set — the chart, grid, toolbar and tabs are byte-for-byte the same components. What Dave will see is a fuller first screen, which instrument A does not score and instrument B does.
  3. The blind arm regressed for a reason unrelated to the edit. The blind splice carried Tabs.reference.html L80 (.tabs{width:var(--demo-width,640px)}) and L120 (.panel{max-width:52ch}); the wall inherited a 52ch panel and the container query resolved to ONE column (probe: cols 1, rows 6, chart y 1554.4). The #246 blind arm did not hit this because that builder wrote a .tpl-tabs .tabs{width:100%} harness rule blind and this one did not. Blind-arm variance of one harness line is larger than the edit's effect — a measurement finding for W7's four-arm re-run.
  4. A copy-range defect in the sighted protocol, corrected here: the baseline log records toolbar CSS as L34-251; L251 leaves the @container (max-width:400px) block open and every later rule nests inside it — the Tabs CSS silently never applied. L252 is the closing brace. Probe: render-it1-1440-light.png first pass (bare tabs) vs second.
  5. DP-08 is met by slot and missed by content on 2 of 6 tiles — the specimen's own "Awaiting approval" / "Undrawn facilities" carry a count and a status in the delta slot (page L283, L309; snippet L899, L925). Lane D declared it and left it; it is RSQ 2 below.
  6. DP-22 is the loudest miss on the fuller first screen: with six coloured deltas visible at once, two falling-is-good metrics wear red (L270 payments out, L296 FX exposure). The row made the polarity gap more visible, not worse — the baseline had the same binding on four tiles.
  7. The narrow band pays for the wide band. Lane D's 520px reading: first chart 1081.6 → 1368.6 (+287). Recorded in the ledger; not a W1 fix.
  8. Relabel miss: the multi-series markers' aria-labels still say "Current / Savings / Investments" (tooltip "A · Current · Jan: 12", drive chart_tooltip) while legend, table and title say EUR / USD / GBP. Both arms. A believability defect a screen-reader user would hear.
  9. Gate side effect, restored: _validate_screen.py wrote knowledge/_SCREEN-GATE.md and knowledge/_screen-gate/dashboard.md on every run; _SCREEN-GATE.md restored via git show HEAD: after the last run (diff 0 lines); _screen-gate/dashboard.md was untracked before this lane and is left as found.

08 · Ruling-shaped questions

Dave's, not the lane's

  1. Does W1 count as "moved"? The plan's one-line verdict is moved / did not move. The fold moved (−159px, +2 tiles, chart canvas whole); instrument A did not (2/2/0/2 → 2/2/0/2). (a) moved — the fold is the finding · (b) did not move — richness is the instrument · (c) add a fold row to instrument A for W2+. Not recommended either way; the instruments are his.
  2. The two status tiles in the headline row (DP-08): (a) leave as specimens · (b) signed delta vs a period · (c) demote to Stat cards — lane D's RSQ 4, re-asked because the sheet scores DP-08 missed on them.
  3. Six or four — lane D's RSQ 1 stands; this page adds one fact: at 1440 six compact tiles read as one band 150px tall, and the judge's verdict (outputs/w1-density/judge/verdict.md) is the blind reading of it.
  4. Blind-arm harness variance (finding 3): should the Tabs snippet's demo width (L80) and panel cap (L120) move under the snippet's own DEMO CHROME marker so a blind splice can cut it out, or is that W7's problem? (a) a demo-chrome marker on Tabs, a snippet edit · (b) leave; W7 measures it · (c) add "drop every snippet's demo width" to generate-from-canon rule 2. Recommend (a) — it is the same class as the demo-bar the bento template already fences.
  5. The 520px cost (ledger row 2) — lane D's RSQ 2 stands; nothing new here.
